Write a Dockerfile from the renv lockfile

Source: R/write-dockerfile.R
write_dockerfile.Rd

write_dockerfile() reads the renv lockfile of a site set up with renv and writes a Dockerfile and a .dockerignore into the site folder. On this page, renv.lock is that lockfile: renv.lock in the site folder, or the lockfile of the renv profile that renv would pick, as the section "renv profiles" below says. The image that Docker builds from them holds the R version and the R packages that renv.lock records, and the Quarto version that you give. You can then render a report in the image with the site folder mounted, so that its code runs with those versions on another machine that runs Docker with Linux containers on an amd64 processor, or on arm64 for R 4.1.0 or later, the platforms of the Rocker images. renv.lock must record R 4.0.0 or later, because older rocker/r-ver images lack the Rocker scripts that the build runs. The Dockerfile was built and run with rocker/r-ver:4.6.1 on arm64 (Docker 29.9.1, 2026-10-22); older images and amd64 were not built. supplement never runs Docker itself.

Usage

write_dockerfile(path = ".", quarto, digest = NULL, overwrite = FALSE)

Arguments

path

The site folder.

quarto

The Quarto version to install, as three whole numbers joined by ., such as "1.10.19". quarto --version in a terminal prints the version that you render with.

digest

NULL, or the digest of the base image, "sha256:" and 64 lowercase hex digits. With a digest, the FROM line names the image by its tag and the digest, so the build uses that image even after the tag moves.

overwrite

If TRUE, replace an existing Dockerfile and .dockerignore.

Value

The paths of the written Dockerfile and .dockerignore, invisibly.

Details

The Dockerfile starts from the Rocker image rocker/r-ver with the R version in renv.lock, and installs Quarto with Rocker's install_quarto.sh. It copies renv.lock into the image. It downloads the renv version that renv.lock records from the CRAN archive of Posit Package Manager (p3m.dev), installs it into a temporary library, uses it to install the Ubuntu packages that renv::sysreqs() lists for the packages in renv.lock, and runs renv::restore(). renv reads those packages from renv.lock from version 1.3.1 on, so renv.lock must record renv 1.3.1 or later. The packages, renv included, go into a library in the image under /opt/renv/library, which RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY names. renv's package cache is off, so the library holds the packages and not links into a cache. When the site folder is mounted at /site, the site's renv/activate.R loads renv from that library, with no download.

The .dockerignore holds two lines: *, and ! with the path of renv.lock from the site folder, such as !renv.lock. So of the site's files only renv.lock can be copied into the image. The image holds no other site file and no data. Both files are written with LF line endings on every system.

renv profiles

An renv profile is a named set of packages with a lockfile of its own. write_dockerfile() picks the profile by the rule of renv 1.3.1, which check_supplement(renv_lock = TRUE) also uses. It does not read RENV_PATHS_LOCKFILE or RENV_PATHS_RENV. If the RENV_PROFILE environment variable of the R session that runs write_dockerfile() is not empty, it names the profile. Otherwise the first line of renv/profile in the site folder names it, when that file exists. The name default, an empty name, or no name means no profile, and the lockfile is renv.lock in the site folder. With a profile, the lockfile is renv/profiles/<name>/renv.lock, and the function prints a message that names the lockfile, the profile, and where the name came from. When RENV_PROFILE and the first line of renv/profile give the same name, as in an R session that the site's renv/activate.R started, because it copies that line into RENV_PROFILE, the message names both.

With a profile, the .dockerignore lets that lockfile into the image. The Dockerfile copies it to the same path and sets the RENV_PROFILE environment variable of the image to the name. renv keeps the packages of a profile in a library of their own, so the build restores them there, and each render in the image uses the profile, whatever renv/profile in the mounted site folder names. The name must hold only ASCII letters, digits, ., _, and -, and must not start with ., so that the Dockerfile can hold it. Each folder and file in the path renv/profiles/<name>/renv.lock must have that letter case, as renv.lock must without a profile, because Docker matches file names with letter case.

Build and render

In a terminal, in the site folder, build the image and give it a name:

docker build -t my-supplement .

Then render one report in it with the site folder mounted at /site. On macOS and Linux:

docker run --rm --network none --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -e HOME=/tmp \
  -v "$PWD":/site my-supplement quarto render analyses/example.qmd

--network none shows that the render needs nothing from the network. --user runs the render as you. On Linux it makes you the owner of the files that the render writes into the site folder; Docker Desktop on macOS does that without it. HOME=/tmp gives that user a home folder in the container.

Versions that can change

An image tag such as rocker/r-ver:4.6.1 can be moved to a newer image, so without digest, a later build can get newer system libraries. To pin the base image, read the digest of its multi-platform index:

docker buildx imagetools inspect rocker/r-ver:4.6.1

and pass the Digest: value, such as "sha256:bafb...", as digest. The build also installs Ubuntu packages for the R packages. These come from Ubuntu's package archive at build time, so they can be newer in a later build even with digest.

To keep the built image itself, write it to a file that you can archive:

docker save -o my-supplement.tar my-supplement

docker load -i my-supplement.tar reads it back. Commit the Dockerfile and the .dockerignore: the Zenodo archive of a GitHub release then holds them, but not the image.

Errors

The function checks the arguments, renv/profile, renv.lock, and both target paths before it writes a file, so after any error but a failed write the site folder is as it was. It writes .dockerignore first, then the Dockerfile. A failed write, an open that fails included, can leave .dockerignore written, and either file empty or cut short. A file that cannot be opened for writing gives R's own error. The other errors have the class supplement_error and one of these classes:

  • supplement_error_argument: path is not a single non-missing, non-empty string, or it is not a folder. quarto is missing or is not one string of three whole numbers joined by ., each 0 or without a leading zero. digest is not NULL or one string of sha256: and 64 lowercase hex digits. overwrite is not TRUE or FALSE.

  • supplement_error_profile: renv/profile is read and is a folder or a file that cannot be opened, or the profile name holds a character other than an ASCII letter, a digit, ., _, or -, or starts with .. The name check comes before any check of a lockfile.

  • supplement_error_no_file: the folder has no renv.lock, or renv.lock is a folder or a link to a missing file. This is also the error when renv.lock, or with a profile a folder or file in the path renv/profiles/<name>/renv.lock, is listed under another spelling, such as another letter case.

  • supplement_error_lockfile: renv.lock is not a JSON object, has no R object with a Version, or has no renv entry with a Version under Packages, or one of the two versions is not one string of three whole numbers joined by .. A development version such as 1.1.5.9000 is such an error, because the build installs released versions. An R version older than 4.0.0 or a renv version older than 1.3.1 is also this error. So is a key that the function reads, given twice in the same object: R or Packages at the top level, Version in R, renv in Packages, or Version in that renv entry. This check comes before the version checks.

  • supplement_error_file_exists: Dockerfile or .dockerignore exists and overwrite is FALSE. A folder at either path is this error even when overwrite is TRUE. So is a link, also a link to a missing file, because a write would follow it.

  • supplement_error_write: a file was opened, but writing it gave an error or a warning, or the file then has another size than the text.

See also

The parts "Recording R packages with renv" and "Running reports in a container" of the template guide, GUIDE.md.

Examples

site <- file.path(tempdir(), "my-supplement")
dir.create(site)
writeLines(
  '{"R": {"Version": "4.6.1"}, "Packages": {"renv": {"Version": "1.3.1"}}}',
  file.path(site, "renv.lock")
)
write_dockerfile(site, quarto = "1.10.19")
readLines(file.path(site, "Dockerfile"))
#>  [1] "# Written by supplement::write_dockerfile() from renv.lock. See"                                                                                                     
#>  [2] "# ?supplement::write_dockerfile for how to build the image and render in it."                                                                                        
#>  [3] "FROM rocker/r-ver:4.6.1"                                                                                                                                             
#>  [4] ""                                                                                                                                                                    
#>  [5] "# renv installs the packages into a library under /opt/renv/library, with"                                                                                           
#>  [6] "# its package cache off, and the site's renv/activate.R finds them there."                                                                                           
#>  [7] "ENV RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY=/opt/renv/library \\"                                                                                                                         
#>  [8] "    RENV_CONFIG_CACHE_ENABLED=FALSE"                                                                                                                                 
#>  [9] ""                                                                                                                                                                    
#> [10] "RUN /rocker_scripts/install_quarto.sh 1.10.19"                                                                                                                       
#> [11] ""                                                                                                                                                                    
#> [12] "# A temporary copy of renv 1.3.1 installs the system packages that the R"                                                                                            
#> [13] "# packages need, then restores renv.lock, renv itself included."                                                                                                     
#> [14] "WORKDIR /opt/renv"                                                                                                                                                   
#> [15] "COPY renv.lock renv.lock"                                                                                                                                            
#> [16] "RUN apt-get update \\"                                                                                                                                               
#> [17] "    && export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive R_LIBS=/tmp/renv/library RENV_PATHS_ROOT=/tmp/renv/root \\"                                                             
#> [18] "    && mkdir -p \"$R_LIBS\" \\"                                                                                                                                      
#> [19] "    && Rscript -e 'install.packages(\"https://p3m.dev/cran/latest/src/contrib/Archive/renv/renv_1.3.1.tar.gz\", repos = NULL, type = \"source\"); library(renv)' \\" 
#> [20] "    && Rscript -e 'writeLines(as.character(unique(unlist(lapply(renv::sysreqs(report = FALSE, check = FALSE), `[[`, \"packages\")))), \"/tmp/renv/sysreqs.txt\")' \\"
#> [21] "    && xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/renv/sysreqs.txt \\"                                                                               
#> [22] "    && Rscript -e 'renv::restore(library = renv::paths$library(), prompt = FALSE)' \\"                                                                               
#> [23] "    && rm -rf /tmp/renv /var/lib/apt/lists/*"                                                                                                                        
#> [24] ""                                                                                                                                                                    
#> [25] "WORKDIR /site"                                                                                                                                                       
unlink(site, recursive = TRUE)
